name: fastjson-1.2.83-deser
notes: The expectation is `deserialization-sink`, not `confirmed`, and the
distinction is the point of the tier. A callback proves the application
reconstructed an object graph RCEKit supplied -- fastjson resolved the type
name and instantiated it. Reaching execution from there depends on gadgets
on the classpath, which this gadget deliberately does not carry: URLDNS
resolves a name and does nothing else. A case expecting `confirmed` here
would be asserting the promotion the tier rule forbids.
The control is class attribution. The payload reaches fastjson either way --
in the control it arrives as a JSON string value the parser reads -- and
`eval` must come back `negative`, because parsing an object graph is not
evaluating an expression. If it ever confirms, `deser` is measuring
something other than what its name claims.
The shape oracle is not what this case rests on. fastjson answers a
truncated stream exactly as it answers a complete one -- it resolves the
type name before the parse finishes -- so the shape differential reports
`negative` here by design, and the DNS gadget is what reaches the tier.
Why the run happens inside a container: the gadget's only channel is a name
lookup, so RCEKit's listener has to own UDP 53 on an address the target's
resolver uses. Inside the target's own network that port is free.
